original_visible_content.stem: A less expensive drug product is reasonably available and appears on the Massachusetts interchangeable-drug list, but the prescription contains a valid prescriber no-substitution direction. Which statements correctly describe the product-selection decision? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The valid no-substitution direction prevents the pharmacist from applying the usual required interchange on this prescription.
A lower price does not override a valid prescriber no-substitution direction.

Without a valid no-substitution direction, the Massachusetts interchange framework generally requires use of the reasonably available, less expensive interchangeable product when its conditions are met.
The patient may erase the prescriber's valid no-substitution direction and compel interchange without prescriber involvement.
Before interchanging, the pharmacist must still confirm that the alternative satisfies the Massachusetts interchangeable-product framework rather than relying on price alone.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts product selection depends on interchange eligibility, price/availability conditions, and the prescriber's substitution direction. A valid no-substitution instruction controls despite a lower price and blocks the otherwise applicable interchange rule. When substitution is permitted, the pharmacist still must use a legally interchangeable product rather than treating lower price alone as sufficient.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. A valid prescriber no-substitution direction is a controlling exception to interchange.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. Lower price does not nullify a valid no-substitution instruction.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. In the absence of a valid no-substitution instruction, the statutory interchange conditions apply.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The patient cannot simply erase the prescriber's valid direction and convert it into a substitution-authorized prescription.
choice_analysis.E: Correct. Price is not enough by itself; the selected alternative must satisfy the governing interchangeable-product requirements.

related_facts: Product-selection law belongs to the NABP Area-4 practice-operations competency rather than prescription-transfer/dispensing mechanics.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not let price or inventory status override a valid prescriber no-substitution direction.

original_visible_content.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy licensed for sterile compounding prepares a patient-specific sterile compounded infusion for outpatient use. The ordinary prescription label is complete, but the final container does not identify the preparation as compounded and does not display the pharmacy's required pharmacist-contact telephone number. What should happen before the product leaves the pharmacy?

choices.text: Dispense it because ordinary prescription-label elements make all compounded-product labeling requirements optional.
Remove the ordinary prescription label and use only the word 'sterile' on the container.
Correct the container to identify the sterile compounded preparation and include the required pharmacist-contact information before outpatient dispensing.
Dispense it unchanged if the patient has previously received another compounded medication from the pharmacy.
Treat the missing information only as a continuing-education issue for the compounding pharmacist.

explanation.core_reasoning: The pharmacy must verify the compounded product itself, not just the prescription. Massachusetts adds a compounded-preparation designation and, for covered sterile/complex nonsterile compounding pharmacies, required pharmacist contact information for outpatient products.

choice_analysis.A: Massachusetts imposes additional compounded-preparation labeling and, for covered pharmacies, pharmacist-contact requirements.
choice_analysis.B: The additional compounded-product information supplements rather than replaces ordinary applicable labeling duties.
choice_analysis.C: The facts describe a covered outpatient sterile compounded preparation missing the additional statutory label/contact elements.
choice_analysis.D: Prior patient experience does not waive the product-specific label and communication requirements.
choice_analysis.E: The defect is on the dispensed product and communication label, not merely the pharmacist's CE record.

related_facts: Compounded-drug labeling is distinct from compounding CE.
The institutional inpatient exception does not fit an outpatient dispensing.
explanation.mpje_trap: A complete ordinary prescription label can still be incomplete for a compounded preparation.

original_visible_content.stem: A valid chlamydia-partner prescription uses 'EPT' instead of a partner name and address. The pharmacist decides to fill it. How should the pharmacy handle the patient profile and prescription label?

choices.text: Create the profile and label using the EPT designation in place of the partner's name and address.
Use the index patient's profile and label so no new record exists.
Use the prescriber's name as the patient identifier.
Dispense with no patient profile because EPT prescriptions are exempt from pharmacy records.
Invent a fictitious first and last name for the partner.

explanation.core_reasoning: The pharmacy creates a separate profile and label using an approved EPT designation.

choice_analysis.A: That is the instructed anonymous EPT workflow.
choice_analysis.B: The partner prescription gets its own EPT record.
choice_analysis.C: The prescriber does not replace the partner identifier.
choice_analysis.D: The policy instructs creation of a profile.
choice_analysis.E: The EPT designation is the permitted identifier.

related_facts: Anonymous EPT does not eliminate the pharmacy record.
explanation.mpje_trap: Using the index patient's identity for the partner's prescription.

original_visible_content.stem: Assume each prescription is otherwise valid and the pharmacist has completed all required training. Which Massachusetts pharmacist-administration scenarios fall within a current authorized category? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Administer patient-specific Vivitrol for substance use disorder under the applicable prescriber-directed guidance
Administer patient-specific Abilify Maintena for mental illness under the applicable guidance
Administer testosterone cypionate for routine hypogonadism solely because the same product is authorized for gender-affirming care
Administer insulin glargine for diabetes solely because it is a prescription Schedule VI product
Administer prescribed testosterone cypionate for gender-affirming care

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts pharmacist administration is driven by an authorized product/indication pathway, not by prescription status alone.

choice_analysis.A: Extended-release naltrexone is an eligible SUD product.
choice_analysis.B: The listed LAI pathway covers this product.
choice_analysis.C: The statutory indication matters.
choice_analysis.D: Schedule VI status alone creates no general injection authority.
choice_analysis.E: Gender-affirming testosterone is an express administration category.

related_facts: MH/SUD products remain subject to the detailed administration guidance.
explanation.mpje_trap: Recognizing an injectable product but ignoring the legally material indication.

original_visible_content.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives several prescriptions for testosterone cypionate. Which scenarios fit the current statutory pharmacist-administration category specifically because of the indication? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A veterinarian's testosterone order for an animal, relying on the human gender-affirming administration provision
A prescribed dose for gender-affirming care
A subsequent prescribed gender-affirming dose after the pharmacist verifies the same authorized pathway remains satisfied
A prescribed dose for routine testosterone-replacement therapy for hypogonadism, relying only on the gender-affirming statute
A bodybuilding request with no valid prescription

explanation.core_reasoning: For this pharmacist-administration authority, gender-affirming indication is legally material even though the testosterone product is unchanged.

choice_analysis.A: The cited human pharmacist-administration category does not fit.
choice_analysis.B: That indication is expressly included.
choice_analysis.C: The category is indication-based, not limited to a single first dose.
choice_analysis.D: That is a different indication.
choice_analysis.E: Neither indication nor prescription authority is satisfied.

related_facts: Testosterone remains federally Schedule III regardless of this administration category.
explanation.mpje_trap: Letting one authorized use of a drug create blanket administration authority for all uses.

original_visible_content.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is preparing a new prescription for delivery to a patient's home. To satisfy the counseling-offer requirement for off-site delivery, the pharmacy provides access to its toll-free service that connects the patient with a pharmacist. Before the prescription is sent, which additional step is required under Massachusetts law?

choices.text: Print the toll-free service number on a label affixed to each prescription drug container.
Place the number only on the outer shipping package, as long as it remains visible until opening.
Include the number only on the delivery receipt that the patient signs.
Send the number in an electronic message after the package has been delivered.
Replace the toll-free number with the dispensing pharmacy's ordinary local number on the container label.

explanation.core_reasoning: When a patient elects delivery at a location other than a pharmacy, M.G.L. c.94C, §21A allows the section's requirements to be satisfied by access to a toll-free telephone service facilitating communication with the pharmacist. The statute also requires that toll-free service number to be printed on a label affixed to each prescription drug container. Outer-package, receipt, post-delivery message, or local-number substitutes do not meet that specified container-label step.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. Section 21A requires the toll-free service number on a label affixed to each prescription drug container for off-site delivery.
choice_analysis.B: The statute specifies the prescription drug container label, not only the outer shipping package.
choice_analysis.C: A delivery receipt does not substitute for the required label on each prescription drug container.
choice_analysis.D: Sending the number after delivery does not satisfy the required container-label placement before the prescription reaches the patient.
choice_analysis.E: The statute calls for the toll-free service number used for this remote counseling-access pathway; an ordinary local number is not the specified substitute.

explanation.mpje_trap: Do not confuse supplying remote telephone access with placing the required toll-free number on each prescription container.

original_visible_content.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist receives a prescription for a brand-name biological product. The prescriber has not prohibited substitution. The pharmacy has a less expensive FDA-licensed biosimilar, but FDA has not determined that product to be interchangeable with the prescribed biologic. May the pharmacist substitute that biosimilar under Massachusetts' statutory biologic-substitution authority without obtaining new prescriber authorization?

choices.text: Yes, because every FDA-licensed biosimilar is automatically interchangeable for pharmacy substitution.
Yes, because the absence of a prescriber prohibition is the only condition Massachusetts imposes.
No. The statutory substitution pathway requires an FDA determination that the substitute is interchangeable with the prescribed biological product.
No, because Massachusetts prohibits pharmacist substitution of any biological product.
Yes, but only if the patient waives notification to the prescriber.

explanation.core_reasoning: M.G.L. c.112, §12EE authorizes pharmacist substitution when FDA has determined the biological product is interchangeable with the prescribed brand-name biological product and the prescriber has not prohibited substitution. Biosimilar licensure alone does not satisfy the interchangeable-product condition.

choice_analysis.A: Biosimilar status does not automatically establish interchangeability for this statutory pathway.
choice_analysis.B: Absence of a prescriber prohibition is necessary but not sufficient.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: FDA interchangeability is a statutory condition for pharmacist substitution.
choice_analysis.D: Massachusetts permits substitution when the statutory conditions are met.
choice_analysis.E: Patient waiver does not replace the required interchangeability determination.

explanation.mpje_trap: Do not treat 'biosimilar' and 'interchangeable' as synonyms.

original_visible_content.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is filling a written prescription for a controlled substance dispensed as capsules. Which items must appear on the label the pharmacist affixes to the container? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The prescribing practitioner's registration number.
The filling pharmacist's initials.
The serial number of the prescription.
The number of capsules in the container.
The date of filling, and the pharmacy name and address.

explanation.core_reasoning: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21 requires the pharmacist filling a controlled-substance prescription to affix a label showing the date of filling, the pharmacy name and address, the FILLING PHARMACIST'S INITIALS, the SERIAL NUMBER of the prescription, the patient's name, the prescribing practitioner's name, the name of the controlled substance, directions and cautionary statements, and where dispensed as tablets or capsules the NUMBER of them in the container. The practitioner's registration number belongs on the prescription under s. 22, not on the pharmacist's label.

choice_analysis.A: That is a prescription requirement under s. 22, not a label requirement.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the filling pharmacist's initials.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: the prescription serial number.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the count is required for tablets and capsules.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: date of filling with pharmacy name and address.

related_facts: The practitioner's own dispensing label is governed separately by s. 22(b)
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates merge the prescription contents and the label contents into a single list.

original_visible_content.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy licensed for sterile compounding prepares two products on the same morning: a sterile infusion for an outpatient, and a sterile preparation for a patient admitted as an inpatient in the same hospital under its institutional licence. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Both containers must be labelled as a sterile compounded preparation.
The outpatient container must also carry the pharmacist-contact telephone number.
The telephone must be staffed during regular hours of operation and at least 56 hours a week.
The inpatient preparation must also carry the telephone number, since the pharmacy does sterile compounding.
The pharmacist reachable on that number must have access to the patient's records.

explanation.core_reasoning: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21 sets two distinct duties. All drug preparations compounded by a board-licensed pharmacy must carry a label notifying users and practitioners that the drug is a sterile or non-sterile compounded preparation. Separately, pharmacies engaged in sterile or complex non-sterile compounding must provide a telephone number fostering communication between patients and a pharmacist employed by the pharmacy who has access to the patient's records, staffed during regular hours of operation every day and not less than 56 hours per week, affixed to the container alongside the compounded-preparation label. That telephone paragraph does not apply to an institutional pharmacy licensed under c. 112, s. 39I where the sterile preparation is to be administered to an inpatient within the same hospital.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the compounded-preparation label duty reaches all such preparations.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: the outpatient container falls squarely within the telephone paragraph.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: staffed during regular hours every day and not less than 56 hours per week.
choice_analysis.D: The telephone paragraph is disapplied for an inpatient preparation within the same hospital.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the pharmacist reached must have access to the patient's records.

related_facts: The carve-out is tied to administration within the same hospital, not merely to inpatient status
explanation.mpje_trap: One exception is written into one of the two paragraphs. Reading it as an exception to both strips the required compounded-preparation label from the inpatient container.

original_visible_content.stem:
A Massachusetts pharmacist reviews outpatient labels and proposed substitutions. Assume the prescriber’s intended ingredient, strength, dosage form, and route are known. Each option describes a separate work-queue record. Assume all other prerequisites are satisfied; judge the action and facts actually stated, not an unstated exception.

Which ONE proposed handling is supported by the applicable requirements?

choices.text: A pharmacist distinguishes an authorized generic marketed under the brand NDA from a separate ANDA product.
A pharmacist changes an immediate-release prescription to an extended-release product with the same ingredient and strength without clarification.
A pharmacist refuses an otherwise lawful pharmacy-to-pharmacy transfer based on the patient label’s federal transfer warning.
A pharmacist gives a reconstituted medication a one-year label date without considering its shorter in-use limit.

explanation.core_reasoning: 각 선택지는 별도 기록이다. 같은 약·업무 이름보다 자격, 실제 행위, 시작점과 예외를 비교한다. Manufacturer expiry, BUD/in-use period, 일반 date ceiling 중 실제 적용되는 더 짧은 제한을 지킨다. Ingredient 뿐 아니라 strength/form/route/TE relationship 및 처방 의도를 확인한다. IR/ER 는 자동 대체가 아니다. Regulatory product relationship 을 확인한다. 같은 회사라는 이유만으로 authorized generic 을 추정하지 않는다. Label 의 다른 사람에게 약물 양도 금지와 pharmacist prescription-information transfer 는 다른 의미이다.

choice_analysis.A: 선택할 항목. Regulatory product relationship 을 확인한다. 같은 회사라는 이유만으로 authorized generic 을 추정하지 않는다.
choice_analysis.B: 선택하지 않을 항목. Ingredient 뿐 아니라 strength/form/route/TE relationship 및 처방 의도를 확인한다. IR/ER 는 자동 대체가 아니다. 올바른 처리: A pharmacist evaluates an exact product’s therapeutic-equivalence relationship rather than relying only on the active ingredient name.
choice_analysis.C: 선택하지 않을 항목. Label 의 다른 사람에게 약물 양도 금지와 pharmacist prescription-information transfer 는 다른 의미이다. 올바른 처리: A pharmacist recognizes that a required federal patient-to-patient transfer warning does not prohibit a lawful pharmacy-to-pharmacy prescription-information transfer.
choice_analysis.D: 선택하지 않을 항목. Manufacturer expiry, BUD/in-use period, 일반 date ceiling 중 실제 적용되는 더 짧은 제한을 지킨다. 올바른 처리: A pharmacist applies a shorter product-specific in-use period when it is more limiting than the general label-date ceiling.

explanation.learning_boundary: 같은 모델의 9개 문항은 조건·기록 조합을 바꾸는 연습 변형이다. 독립된 9개 법규나 실제 기출로 세지 않으며, 세트에는 모델별 한 문항만 선택한다.
